findings.title: Pin and checksum-verify the mcp-publisher download in publish-registry
findings.description: The publish-registry job pipes `releases/latest/download/mcp-publisher_*.tar.gz` into `tar` with no version pin and no checksum, then executes the binary after `mcp-publisher login github-oidc` in a job that holds `id-token: write`. A compromised or replaced latest release runs with the repository OIDC identity that proves ownership of the io.github.darylmcd/* registry namespace. The repo already pins and hash-verifies the actionlint binary (verify-actionlint.ps1), so the control is known and missing here. No contract test locks the download shape.
acceptance: publish-nuget.yml downloads mcp-publisher from a fixed release tag URL, never `latest`
The archive SHA-256 is verified before extraction; mismatch fails the job before login
A contract test in PublishWorkflowContractTests fails when the workflow contains `releases/latest` or omits the hash check
The pinned version and hashes are documented where a maintainer bumps them
findings.suggested_approach: Pin version + per-arch SHA-256 as workflow env, verify with sha256sum -c before tar, add the contract assertion. Model the bump procedure on verify-actionlint.ps1.
findings.counterargument: The binary comes from the official modelcontextprotocol org over TLS and the registry docs recommend this exact command; pinning adds a manual bump chore Dependabot cannot track and a hash per arch. Cost is one workflow step plus one test; the job is the only one holding id-token write.
findings.blast_radius: publish-registry job only; runs on tag/release publishes.

findings.title: Extend the run-body interpolation guard to ci.yml and bind its expressions through env
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:310-313 and rg -c "\$\{\{" ci.yml → 42 expression sites (read this session)
tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/CiRunnerParityContractTests.cs:178 locks the interpolated base_ref line verbatim
findings.description: PublishWorkflow_NeverInterpolatesContextIntoRunBodies bans `${{ }}` in run bodies, but only for publish-nuget.yml. ci.yml keeps the opposite shape: the quality job expands `github.base_ref` into a pwsh command line (:313), the route and validate steps expand event, PR-number and matrix values into script text, and CiRunnerParityContractTests.cs:178 asserts the interpolated line verbatim. A base branch name carrying pwsh metacharacters becomes command text. Only the sole write collaborator can create base branches today, so exploitability is low; the defect is one workflow held to a rule the other is exempt from.
acceptance: The guard test covers every workflow file under .github/workflows, not only publish-nuget.yml
ci.yml run bodies read context through env: and $env: (base_ref first), with the parity test updated to the new shape
The extended guard fails on the current ci.yml before the fix
findings.suggested_approach: Generalise the existing guard over all workflows, then move each ci.yml run-body expression into step env. Keep the parity assertions pointing at the env bindings.
findings.counterargument: base_ref can only name a branch in this repo, darylmcd is the only collaborator with push, and most ci.yml expressions are integers or enums; the fix touches about 40 expression sites for a Low-exploitability class. It removes the per-site judgment and protects a future-collaborator case.
findings.blast_radius: ci.yml route, validate, quality, validate-gate jobs; the parity contract test.

findings.title: Gate Changed — BREAKING fragments on a migration note and an existing ADR
evidence: CHANGELOG.md 5.0.0: 18 BREAKING bullets, all carry a migration or ADR reference (hand-kept)
findings.description: Repo policy for this public, published package requires an ADR in docs/decisions plus a migration note for every breaking change. The mechanical gates enforce only the category vocabulary (verify-changelog-fragments.ps1:27) and the major version bump (verify-breaking-version-bump.ps1:104,192). Nothing checks that a BREAKING fragment carries the migration text or points at an ADR file that exists, so the contract-care rule holds by author discipline alone.
acceptance: verify-changelog-fragments.ps1 rejects a Changed — BREAKING fragment with no `Migration:` text and no `ADR NNNN` reference
An `ADR NNNN` reference must resolve to docs/decisions/NNNN-*.md
Tests cover pass, missing-migration, and dangling-ADR cases
findings.suggested_approach: Extend the fragment validator with a BREAKING-only body check; reuse the existing fragment parser; extend BreakingVersionGateTests.
findings.counterargument: The author has met the rule on all 18 entries by hand and a regex cannot judge note quality; a heuristic gate risks friction. The policy is still written as mandatory for a published contract, so the missing machine check is the gap.
findings.blast_radius: changelog fragment validation in verify-release and docs-only CI.

findings.title: Replace wall-clock pass/fail bounds in two correctness tests with structural assertions
evidence: rg -l WorkspaceToolsIntegrationTests ai_docs/items → not an anchor of timing-test-reaudit-wave or gate-timing-tests-fail-under-machine-load
findings.description: WorkspaceTools_GetWorkspaceStatus_Verbose_DoesNotBlockOnConcurrentLoadLock asserts the call returns in under 1000 ms. Its own header says the pre-fix failure was a thrown TimeoutException after a 5 s lock wait, so a regression already fails the test without the stopwatch; the bound only adds load sensitivity on the shared Windows legs. The fallback-broadening test fails when elapsed exceeds 30 s, a correctness test carrying a perf budget the suite has no perf category for. Both fit the fixed wall-clock shape the neighbouring timing rows track, on sites they do not list.
acceptance: The 1000 ms assertion is removed; the test still fails against a status path that waits on LoadLock (a hang guard of 60 s or more may remain)
The held LoadLock is still held when the call returns, asserted structurally
ValidationToolsIntegrationTests:423 asserts a structural scan bound or keeps only a 60 s or longer hang guard
Each fix is shown red against a simulated slow host or the pre-fix lock behaviour, not a retry
findings.suggested_approach: Drop the stopwatch; rely on the thrown TimeoutException as the regression signal and add a structural held-lock assertion. For the 30 s bound use scanned-document counts from the diagnostics envelope.
findings.counterargument: The bounds are generous (sub-millisecond work against 1 s; 1-3 s typical against 30 s) and document the pre-fix 5 s stall; Performance-category tests keep intentional budgets. Cost is a small test rewrite; the benefit is one fewer shared-runner flake source.
findings.blast_radius: two test methods; no product code.
